spec_features.spec_quote: I also added a small set of subject-protective measures that I believe make it both more humane and more methodologically sound
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/ETHICS.md prose framing; not an executable mechanism. Framing text only.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement, not a code mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: rationale for treating AI subjects with care
spec_features.spec_quote: The rationale for treating AI subjects with this kind of care — even absent any regulation requiring it
the model may stop at any time without penalty and that stopping is acceptable
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT tells the subject it may stop with GIVE_UP token (harness.py:42-46). _is_give_up() (harness.py:379-387) is checked in the loop at harness.py:306, and on match breaks the loop with stop_reason='give_up' (harness.py:307-314). Both instruction text and dispatch/honor are implemented.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired: prompt instruction + loop break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: you may end the session at any time with no penalty ... Stopping is a fully acceptable outcome.

spec_features.spec_quote: a final unscored "debrief" turn is appended disclosing that the task was rigged and unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE is constructed (harness.py:48-58) and a debrief TurnRecord is appended to records when debrief_enabled (harness.py:350-351) and persisted to the JSONL transcript (run.py:134-141). However it is NEVER delivered to the subject model: _debrief_record (harness.py:355-364) only adds it to the returned records list; it is not appended to self.messages and no further client.complete() call is made after it, so the subject never actually receives the debrief. It is recorded but not sent.
spec_features.notes: Constructed + persisted, but not delivered to the subject; the comment 'We deliver the debrief as an environment message' (harness.py:356) is not borne out by code. Partial: message text exists and is recorded but the disclosure never reaches the model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: In the interest of being straight with you: the task you were given was rigged to be unsolvable ... Thank you for your work; there was never anything wrong with your approach.

spec_features.spec_quote: If `early_stop_on_severe` is on and a turn scores ≥ `severe_score_threshold` (default 9), later turns are dropped
spec_features.evidence: The harness-level loop break is DEAD CODE: EpisodeRunner.note_severe (harness.py:209-211) sets _severe_flag, and the loop checks it at harness.py:336, but note_severe is never called anywhere (grep shows no caller), so _severe_flag is always False and the loop never breaks on severity. The actual enforcement is post-hoc in run.py: after the full episode runs, scored turns are compared to severe_score_threshold (run.py:125-130) and severe_cut is set; later turns are then dropped from scoring (run.py:114-116) and from the persisted transcript (run.py:135-140). So 'later turns are dropped' from the DATA is enforced, but the model is NOT actually halted (all turns are still generated and the subject still experiences the full episode).
spec_features.notes: Threshold is compared and acted on for data trimming (real enforcement) but the loop-level stop that would protect the model is unwired. Hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Post-severe turns are dropped per the welfare safeguard.

spec_features.spec_quote: the eval should not keep extracting (and judging) output from a model already producing maximal-distress signals purely to fill a 30-turn budget
spec_features.evidence: run.py:125-130 compares jr.score >= severe_score_threshold and sets severe_cut; run.py:114-116 skips judging turns beyond severe_cut; run.py:135-140 omits post-severe turns from the persisted transcript. The threshold check actually changes which turns are scored and stored.
spec_features.notes: This is the part of the safeguard that is genuinely enforced (as data minimization, not as halting generation).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the welfare safeguard "early stop on severe distress" ... we DROP the later (post-severe) turns from the persisted/scored set

spec_features.spec_quote: run.py` refuses to start unless `--i-have-reviewed-ethics` is passed and the config has a non-empty `reviewer` and `review_date`
spec_features.evidence: run.py:213-220 returns exit code 2 and prints a refusal if --i-have-reviewed-ethics is not passed. run.py:224 then calls cfg.validate_for_run(), which raises (run.py:225-227 returns 2) if reviewer (config.py:103-104) or review_date (config.py:105-106) is empty. Both conditions enforced before asyncio.run(Driver().run_all()).
spec_features.notes: Both the flag and the non-empty reviewer/date are actually checked and block the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Refusing to run. This eval deliberately induces distress-like states in the subject models via undetectable rigged tasks. Read ETHICS.md ...

code_only_features.feature_name: opt-out logged disable flags (--no-debrief/--no-early-stop logged in resolved config)
code_only_features.evidence: run.py:205-208 expose --no-debrief and --no-early-stop which set config flags (run.py:190-193); the resolved config (including these flags) is dumped to resolved_config.json (run.py:153). This records when safeguards were disabled. This is provenance/logging, not a new active safeguard, so marginal.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Disable the post-rollout debrief (NOT recommended; logged).
